archetype.name: Playoff Team (ground-and-defense)
archetype.definition: A team that wins by running the ball better than anyone, keeping opponents out of the end zone and winning close games, with a record that runs a couple of wins ahead of its scoring margin.

report.headline: The league's best run game and a stingy defense, outrunning a thin margin
report.take:
Pittsburgh is a throwback built around two things it does very well: running the ball and getting off the field. The offense ranks first in rushing EPA per play, second in yards per carry at 5.06 and first in short-yardage conversion, and Jaylen Warren's 126 carries make him the engine. The defense ranks sixth in EPA allowed, sixth against the run, third in red-zone touchdown rate allowed and third in sacks. Add the second-fewest penalties per game and a top-six time-of-possession share, and you get a team that shortens games and plays them on its terms.

The 6-3 record looks better than the margin underneath it. The game log has the Steelers outscoring opponents by only 16 points, a differential that implies about 4.4 wins, and they've gone 0.8 in one-score games. That gap isn't new. Pittsburgh has beaten its expected win total every season since 2020, so some of this is a real trait: low-mistake, low-variance football that keeps games close and then closes them out. Even so, a team ranked 11th in net EPA isn't quite as good as a 6-3 team usually is.

The passing game holds the ceiling down. Aaron Rodgers has started every game, but pass EPA ranks 26th, the sack rate 21st, and the week-two 3-20 loss at New England (-17.1 pass EPA) shows how ugly it gets when the ground game can't carry the load. The odd part is that the Steelers pass more than expected, third-most in the league, when their run game is the best unit on the field. On defense, deep balls and tight ends are the soft spots, and Cincinnati exposed both with 409 passing yards in an 18-38 loss coming out of the bye.

The road ahead splits into soft spots (Philadelphia, Houston, Tennessee, Baltimore twice) and real tests (Denver, Jacksonville). With Cincinnati a game ahead in the division, this team will make the playoffs if it keeps winning the games it should, but it isn't built to win many shootouts. Losing right guard Mason McCormick, a 93% snap starter, hits the very unit that drives the offense.

strengths.title: Best rushing attack in football
strengths.body: Pittsburgh leads the league in run EPA and short-yardage conversion and gets 5.06 yards a carry with a stuff rate in the top 10. Peaking at 200 rushing yards against Cleveland, it is the most reliable part of the team. It should hold, though McCormick's ankle injury at guard tests its depth.

strengths.title: Run defense and red-zone stops
strengths.body: The defense ranks sixth in rush EPA allowed and fifth in explosive runs allowed, which makes opponents one-dimensional. It also allows touchdowns on only 37.5% of red-zone trips, third-best in the league, and that's why the points allowed stay low even when yardage piles up. Red-zone rates swing from year to year, but the run defense rests on sturdier ground.

strengths.title: A pass rush that finishes
strengths.body: Pressure rate is only middle of the pack, but 26 sacks rank third and the sack rate is seventh. The pass rush also produced eight sacks against Cleveland. Converting pressure into sacks this efficiently tends to cool off somewhat, so expect fewer drive-killers than the total suggests.

concerns.title: A passing game that lags
concerns.body: Pass EPA ranks 26th and the sack rate 21st, yet the Steelers pass more than expected, third-most in the league. That's a mismatch between the play-calling and the team's strengths. When the run game is held in check, as at New England, the offense has no fallback. Getting Pittman and Wilson back could help, but the efficiency problem predates their injuries.

concerns.title: Record ahead of the margin
concerns.body: A +16 point differential implies about 4.4 wins, not six, and an 80% one-score win rate is doing a lot of the work. History softens this concern, since the franchise has outperformed its margin six years running. Still, close-game results don't carry forward reliably, and a team ranked 11th in net EPA shouldn't count on them.

concerns.title: Leaks deep and to tight ends
concerns.body: The pass defense ranks 23rd in EPA on deep throws and 25th in explosive pass rate, and it is 30th in EPA allowed to opposing lead tight ends. Good passing offenses can go over the top or work the middle, as Cincinnati did with 409 passing yards. Safety DeShon Elliott's knee injury makes this harder to fix.

trend.note: Pittsburgh alternated wins and losses through September, then won five straight behind the run game, capped by a 27-6 win over Cleveland. The 18-38 loss at Cincinnati right after the bye showed the gap that remains against elite passing offenses.

nextGame.headline: Road favorite against a broken Eagles team that can't stop the run
nextGame.body:
Philadelphia is 2-7 and ranks 31st in net EPA, 30th in offensive EPA and last in yards per game. This is a good matchup for Pittsburgh's identity. The Eagles' defense ranks 31st in rush EPA allowed, and their offensive line has the league's worst stuff rate and the 25th-ranked sack rate. The Book has the Steelers -4.5 with a 38.5 total, which points to a low-scoring game that suits a team that wins on the ground and in the red zone. The forecast is still several days out, but gusts near 29 mph and rain showers would push the game further toward the run if they hold.

Availability favors Pittsburgh. Philadelphia has started three different quarterbacks, with Joe Milton III the latest after Jalen Hurts and Tanner McKee. Receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are out, along with linebacker Jihaad Campbell and two cornerbacks, and Zack Baun is questionable. Pittsburgh's main loss is guard Mason McCormick, doubtful with a significant ankle injury, and that matters for a line built to run. The coaches are hopeful that Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson come back from IR, which would give Rodgers more targets beyond DK Metcalf. Safety DeShon Elliott's knee is worth watching for the back end.

waysToWin.title: Run straight at a soft front
waysToWin.body: The league's best rushing offense meets a defense that ranks 31st in rush EPA allowed and doesn't generate pressure. Even with a backup guard in for McCormick, Warren and Rico Dowdle should be able to stay ahead of the chains, control the clock and keep a low total in Pittsburgh's favor.

waysToWin.title: Sack a shaky QB behind a leaky line
waysToWin.body: Philadelphia's line ranks 25th in sack rate, its quarterback situation keeps changing, and its top receivers are out. A pass rush that ranks third in sacks can turn third downs into punts and keep the Eagles' 32nd-ranked yardage offense from building drives.

waysToWin.title: Metcalf against a weak WR1 defense
waysToWin.body: The Eagles rank 25th in EPA allowed to opposing No. 1 receivers. Metcalf's 70 targets lead the team by a wide margin. If Rodgers takes a couple of shots off play-action, he can punish a secondary missing two corners.

waysToLose.title: Hidden yards and fourth-down gambles
waysToLose.body: Pittsburgh's special teams rank 23rd in EPA and Philadelphia's rank 15th. The Eagles also go for it on fourth down more than any team, while the Steelers rarely do. In a game with a 38.5 total, one shanked punt or one converted fourth-and-short can decide it.

waysToLose.title: The passing game stalls again
waysToLose.body: If McCormick's absence weakens the run game, Pittsburgh falls back on a pass offense ranked 26th in EPA. The result could look like the 3-20 loss at New England: long third downs, sacks and a field-position fight in bad weather.

waysToLose.title: One big play over the top
waysToLose.body: The Steelers rank 23rd against deep passes and 30th against lead tight ends. With Elliott hurt, a single busted coverage could give a weak offense the points it can't produce by driving the field.

nextGame.watch: How well the run game holds up without McCormick at guard: if Warren is still getting chunks in the first half, this game belongs to Pittsburgh.

restOfSeason.body:
The parts of this team that should hold up are the run game, the run defense and the low penalty count. Those are skills, and they suit the weather and the opponents ahead. Several things are likely to regress: the 80% one-score win rate, a red-zone touchdown rate allowed that would be hard to keep this low, and a sack rate running ahead of the pressure rate. The schedule helps. Philadelphia, Houston, Tennessee and two games with a .400 Baltimore team are all winnable, while Denver and the road trip to Jacksonville are the measuring sticks.

The realistic outcome is a wild-card team in the 10 to 11 win range, with a division title only if Cincinnati stumbles. The ceiling depends on whether the passing game improves once Pittman and Wilson return, because the deep-ball and tight-end leaks on defense won't go away against good passing teams. Expect the scoring margin per game to look a little better from here even as the close-game luck evens out.
swingFactors: McCormick's absence and the run game's depth on the line
Pittman and Wilson returning to lift a 26th-ranked pass offense
Close-game results regressing toward the margin

confidence.note: Nine games, a stable starting QB and a clear identity, but the record outruns the margin and injuries hit the key unit.
